evidence: FUNCTION RANDOM used for random number generation
ACCEPT ... FROM TIME and ACCEPT ... FROM CONSOLE
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS, no COMP-3, no IBM-specific extensions

purpose.summary: This is a COBOL implementation of the classic 'Hunt the Wumpus' text adventure game. The player navigates a cave of 20 rooms connected in a dodecahedron-like topology, avoiding hazards (Wumpus, bottomless pits, super bats) and shooting arrows to kill the Wumpus. The program handles cave generation, random placement of hazards, player movement, arrow shooting, and win/loss conditions.

notable_features: FUNCTION RANDOM with seed from system TIME for random number generation
OCCURS clause used for room array and arrow path
UNSTRING for parsing arrow-shoot command input
GOBACK used instead of STOP RUN
Hardcoded cave topology via MOVE literals into ROOM() entries
INITIALIZE used to reset a flag
Subscripted data items (PASSAGE1, PASSAGE2, PASSAGE3, WUMPUS, PIT, BAT) within OCCURS
verdict.notes: The program is clearly a student or hobbyist implementation of Hunt the Wumpus in COBOL. The intro section is a placeholder ('INTRO PLACE HOLDER'). The arrow-shooting loop has a potential infinite loop risk if ARROW-ROOM-COUNT exceeds 5 without hitting a wall or Wumpus. The P-800-DISPLAY-WUMPUS paragraph is empty. No comments are present. The dialect is consistent with GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus but nothing vendor-specific is visible.
